bug_info.bug_desc: In superscalar dual-issue mode, the ALU-ALU bypass logic incorrectly blocks the second instruction when both instructions write the same destination register (WAW hazard). The condition `issue_instr_i[i].rd == issue_instr_i[i-1].rd` checks for a WAW hazard, but the comment and surrounding logic indicate it was intended to handle RAW dependencies. Since WAW hazards are already eliminated by the scoreboard, this redundant check causes a false stall: the second instruction is not acknowledged even though no real data hazard exists and the ALU-ALU bypass is available.
bug_info.fix_hint: Remove the WAW hazard check `(issue_instr_i[i].rd == issue_instr_i[i-1].rd)` from the dual-issue acknowledge logic in `issue_read_operands.sv`. The scoreboard already guarantees WAW elimination, so only the existing RAW hazard logic (`stall_raw`) and the ALU-ALU bypass conditions (`alu_bypass.rs1_from_rd` / `alu_bypass.rs2_from_rd`) are needed to determine if the second instruction can issue.
